en: Now, since in this module I'm going to
compare Deno to Node.js,
we can also have a quick look at how Node.js
works. And for that, on nodejs.org, you
first of all can download and install Node.
It's available for all operating systems. In
case the wrong one was selected for you
here, you can click on other downloads and
find other versions. Now, this will download
the Node.js installer.
You can simply download it
on your system
and then walk through that installer, which
of course is a bit more convenient than the
Deno installation process, I guess, a bit
more what you're used to.
And this will install Node.js, a tool on
your system, and it will also not just
install Node but also npm. So it actually
installs 2 tools.
And npm stands for Node Package Manager, and
it is a tool which will be used in Node apps
to download third-party modules, which you
then can use in your Node app. Because one
key difference, and I'll come back to that,
between Node and Deno will be that for Node,
you have to install and download
dependencies locally,
whereas with Deno, you can import from any
file on any server. But I will come back to
that. One important thing to note, which you
also see here on this page, is that Node.js
is a JavaScript runtime
built on Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine.
And that's almost the same as Deno. Deno
also is a runtime built on Chrome's V8
JavaScript engine. So Deno and Node are 2
technologies with a lot of similarities
which are there to solve the same problem.
Just in different ways. That is really
important.
Now with Node installed here,
we can go into an empty folder and add a new
file, app.js for example. And it should be
JS because Node only works with JavaScript.
And in there, a simple Node script could be
one where you have a message stored in a
constant,
hello there,
And where you then simply console.log this.
And we can then execute this file by running
node and then the file name. So it's not
node run, it's just node and then the file
name.
And you therefore see hello there in the
console thereafter. Now of course you cannot
just write scripts like this with Node. You
can also write scripts that work with the
file system. You can write web servers. You
can do the same things as you can do with
Deno.
So therefore, now that we had this very
brief look at Node and that we installed it,
let's dive into a comparison of Deno and
Node, and let me explain which technology is
better.
